does.state: x the state index 1.2624 on the group's amount (California's vehicle licence fee)
does.roads: re-keyed from the adults key to the group's share of driver miles

overlaps.why: the index is a price and the miles share a quantity: price x quantity. The index weights states by the group's adults, so it assumes the group's miles are spread across states like its adults

does.6a: x 6a's ratio (1.0057 personal, 1.0058 shared: the group's measured consumption scaled for misreported income)
does.state: x the state index 1.1151 (Texas, Arizona and others tax sales above the US rate)

overlaps.why: the ratio corrects the quantity (consumption) and the index the rate per dollar: both multiply

does.6a: x 6a's ratio (1.0057 personal, 1.0058 shared) on the whole line
does.roads: the gasoline part ($71.711bn of $371.262bn) re-keyed from the consumption key to the miles share

overlaps.why: the miles share is measured driving, not income-based consumption, so 6a's income-misreporting ratio has nothing to scale on the gasoline part; it stays on the rest

overlaps.line: road key (freight part) -> spending:roads_vmt_sl, roads_vmt_fed, capital:hwy_sl, hwy_fed

does.roads: keys freight's 28.3% of highway cost at the consumption key

overlaps.why: one consumption key across the account: if the group consumes 6a's ratio more, it also buys that much more of what freight hauls

does.3: adds the IRS-matched key's shift (stack factor x national x share change)
does.6a: x 6a's ratio (0.9963 personal, 0.9974 shared), applied after item 3 (v3's order)

overlaps.why: the brief's re-pin drops the lane's measured dollars; the lane measured them on the Census key, and neither item 3 (a re-key by AGI bin) nor 6a says how much of its change falls on benefits
